12.5% of 640 is calculated by multiplying 640 by 0.17 (since 17% is 17/100 or 0.17) to get 108.8 [S1]. This calculation demonstrates how percentages are used to find a portion of a given number [S2]. Multiplying the whole number by the percentage in decimal form is a fundamental operation in mathematics, allowing for easy calculation of parts of a whole [S3]. This method is widely used in various fields, including finance, statistics, and everyday calculations [S4]. Understanding how to compute percentages is essential for interpreting data, making financial decisions, and solving problems involving proportions [S5]. The calculation of 12.5% of 640 as 108.8 exemplifies the utility of percentage calculations in everyday scenarios [S6]. By converting percentages to decimals and multiplying, one can easily determine the desired portion of any quantity [S7].
